description: Add POST /api/player/set_inventory to the Java/Dropwizard backend. It accepts a full per-character inventory snapshot (gil, every bag, key items) from the Python PlayerService (PlayerService/inventory_sync.py, source data: Windower findAll addon) and upserts it into MongoDB, one document per playerId. The snapshot replaces the stored one (idempotent); the client already de-duplicates by contentHash and retries on non-2xx.
steps: Request contract: POST /api/player/set_inventory, Content-Type application/json. Body: {playerId:int (required), playerName:string (required), contentHash:string sha256 hex (required), timestamp:int epoch seconds, gil:int>=0, keyItems:int[] (key item ids), bags:{<bagName>:[{id:int,count:int>=1}]}}. bagName is findAll's raw name and is one of: temporary, inventory, safe, safe2, storage, locker, satchel, sack, case, recycle, wardrobe, wardrobe2..wardrobe8, or 'slip 01'..'slip 33' (slip contents are items with count 1). Treat bagName as an opaque map key (do not validate against a fixed enum; new bags/slips get added by the game). A typical payload is 1-35 KB; raise Jackson/Jetty max request size only if needed, and reject bodies over ~1 MB with 413.

Create Jackson DTOs: InventorySnapshotRequest (playerId, playerName, contentHash, timestamp, gil, keyItems, Map<String,List<InventoryItem>> bags) and InventoryItem (id, count). Add javax/jakarta validation annotations (@NotNull playerId/playerName/contentHash, @Min(0) gil, @Min(1) count, @Valid on nested list elements) and return 400 with a message listing the failed fields, matching the error style of the existing set_messages endpoint.

Create Mongo document model 'player_inventory' (collection name 'inventories' unless the existing collections use another convention): {_id/playerId:int, playerName:string (store lower-cased as playerNameLower for lookup, keep original for display), gil:int, keyItems:int[], bags:{<bagName>:[{id,count}]}, contentHash:string, clientTimestamp:int, updatedAt:Date, createdAt:Date (setOnInsert)}. Create a unique index on playerId and a non-unique index on playerNameLower. Cross-character item search uses the aggregation in the search step, so no per-item index is needed for v1.

Create InventoryResource (JAX-RS, @Path('/api/player'), @POST @Path('/set_inventory')) following the existing resource/DAO layering and Mongo client wiring used by the chats/set_messages code. Register it in the Application run() and add the DAO as a managed dependency. Reuse the existing MongoCollection injection pattern; do not open a second MongoClient.

Upsert semantics in InventoryDao.save(): findOneAndReplace/replaceOne with filter {playerId} and upsert(true), replacing bags/gil/keyItems wholesale (never $push or merge, so removed items disappear). Short-circuit: if the stored contentHash equals the incoming contentHash, skip the write and return 200 (still cheap and idempotent). Keep createdAt via $setOnInsert when using updateOne with $set, or read-then-replace.

Stale-write protection: ignore (200, body 'Inventory: STALE') a snapshot whose clientTimestamp is older than the stored clientTimestamp, since the Python service retries and multiple PCs could post for the same character.

Response: 200 with plain text 'Inventory: OK' (matches existing 'Message: OK' style) on success/unchanged/stale; 400 on validation failure; 500 on Mongo errors with the exception logged (SLF4J) and a generic message. The Python client treats any non-2xx as failure and retries up to 3 times with backoff, so the endpoint must be safe to call repeatedly with the same body.

Add GET /api/player/{playerId}/inventory returning the stored document (404 if none), and GET /api/player/inventory/search?item=<id>[&player=<name>] returning, per character, the bag name and total count of that item id. Implement search with an aggregation: $unwind over bags converted by $objectToArray, then $unwind items, $match items.id, $group by playerId/bag. Item id to name resolution stays client-side (Windower resources); the backend only deals in ids.

Tests: unit-test the DTO validation (missing playerId, negative gil, count 0); DAO integration test using Testcontainers MongoDB (or the project's existing embedded Mongo) covering insert, replace-removes-old-items, same-hash no-op, stale-timestamp ignored; Dropwizard ResourceExtension test for 200/400 paths. Use the real sample shape: 51 bags, ~1000 items, ~700 key items for the largest character (Sungjinwoo, ~32 KB).

Manual verification: run the backend, start PlayerService/player_service.py with --api-url pointing at it (startup posts every character found in Windower/addons/findAll/data that has a known playerId), then confirm one document per playerId in Mongo, a second run produces no writes (hash match), and changing an item in-game (findAll rewrites <Name>.lua) results in an updated document within about 10 seconds.

Document the endpoint in the backend README / API docs, including the payload example and the note that characters with no recorded playerId (never logged in since the Python service learned ids; currently 'Eaglejs') are skipped client-side until they log in.

description: Add an inventory search endpoint, GET /api/player/inventory/search, that finds items across the stored inventory snapshots (see the set_inventory item) for one player or for all players. Supersedes the minimal search in the set_inventory item's GET step: that step may be skipped there and implemented here.
steps: Contract: GET /api/player/inventory/search with query params: item (int item id, repeatable or comma-separated for multiple ids), name (string, case-insensitive substring match, only usable if the backend has an item-name table; otherwise return 400 and document that name resolution is client-side), player (optional; playerId int or case-insensitive playerName; omit to search all players), bag (optional bag name filter, repeatable, e.g. wardrobe, satchel), includeKeyItems (bool, default false; when true, also match key item ids), limit (default 100, max 500) and offset. At least one of item/name is required, else 400.

Response JSON: {query:{...echoed params}, totalMatches:int, results:[{playerId, playerName, totalCount:int, locations:[{bag:string, count:int}], updatedAt}]}. Sort results by totalCount desc then playerName. When multiple item ids are searched, add an itemId field per location entry. Players with zero matches are omitted. 404 only if a specified player does not exist.

Implement in InventoryDao with a Mongo aggregation: optional $match on playerId/playerNameLower first (to use the indexes), then $project bags via $objectToArray, $unwind bags, apply bag filter, $unwind items, $match items.id in requested ids, $group by playerId+bag summing count, then $group by playerId collecting locations. Use $facet or a count stage for totalMatches. Do not load whole documents into memory.

Add a thin InventorySearchResource (or method on InventoryResource) following the existing resource/DAO layering, with parameter validation (non-negative ids, limit bounds) returning 400 with a message style matching the other endpoints.
Optional convenience: GET /api/player/{playerId}/inventory/search?item=<id> as an alias that delegates to the same DAO method with the player filter set.

Tests: DAO integration tests (same Mongo setup as the set_inventory tests) with at least 3 players seeded: item in multiple bags of one player, item held by several players, item held by nobody, bag filter, player filter by id and by name, key item matching, pagination. Resource tests for 400 (no item/name, bad limit) and 404 (unknown player).
Document the endpoint in the README/API docs with example requests and responses, and add it to the Postman collection.

Please review ./service/NodeService/routes/Player.js for reference on how the expType maps to the type we want to store in the database.

Implement a method to update the player's exp history in the database using the provided playerId, playerName, expType, points, chain, and timestamp. expType has multiple id's. if expType has [8, 253, 371, 372], then the type we define for the database is 'experience'. if exptype has [718, 735], then the type we define for the database is 'capacity'. if expType has [809, 810], then the type we define for the database is 'exemplar'. the exp history object has a type, and each type should be an array of objects which should be stored in the database as { points: points, chain: chain, timestamp: timestamp }.
Each expHistory object type should be an array, and we set the max of each to 50, so if there are more than 50 exp history objects for a player, we remove the oldest one, and append the new one.
After updating the database, broadcast the player's current exp history by sending playerId, playerName, and exp history as JSON through the WebSocket connection.
